abstract.para: In addition to well-known protocols such as http(s)://, ftp://, and file://, &agama; understands most &ay;- and &yast;-specific URL schemes. Use any of these wherever a URL is expected, for example when pointing inst.auto at an unattended installation profile.

section.title: Supported schemes
section.para: &agama; supports the following standard schemes (relying on curl, so a protocol may occasionally work "by accident"; only the schemes documented here are actually supported):

listitem.para: http and https for HTTP and HTTPS.
ftp and ftps for FTP and FTP over TLS.
smb and smbs for the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. Use smb rather than cifs.

section.para: &agama; also supports the following &agama;-specific schemes, described in detail below: , , , and .

section.title: Relative references
section.para: For the url property in the scripts and files sections of an &agama; profile, the value can be a relative reference, resolved against the URL of the profile that contains it. This replaces the relurl scheme used in &ay;.
For example, if the profile below is retrieved from https://example.com/machines/sles16.jsonnet, the script URL resolves to https://example.com/machines/scripts/snapshot.sh:

example.title: Relative script URL in an &agama; installation profile

section.title: &agama;-specific schemes
section.para: Standard protocols cover most use cases, but &agama;-specific schemes can be handy in others. For example, you could distribute a profile on a USB stick instead of over HTTP, with usb:///profile.json, and let &agama; search all attached USB devices for it.
The most flexible scheme, in the general form device://[DEVICE]/PATH.
Search in a specific directory on the same device:
A form of device:// limited to USB devices. Searches profile/sles.json on all attached USB devices:
Searches a file system with a given label, in the form label://LABEL/PATH. For example, search for sles.json on a file system labeled OEMDRV:

section.title: cd, dvd, and hd
section.para: Another particular case of device://, with a slightly different form and no difference in behavior between the three names: dvd:/PATH?devices=DEVICE.

note.title: Prefer device
note.para: Since cd, dvd, and hd offer no advantage over device, prefer device instead.

section.title: Not yet supported
section.para: repo:// URLs are not supported yet, though there are plans to implement them.
